argument_macro_structure.dominant_argument_form: Modus tollens with a constructive synthesis
argument_macro_structure.premise_explicitness: Moderate - premises are embedded in prose but identifiable

argumentative_quality.dialectical_reasonableness: High - engages with counterarguments and provides nuanced resolution
argumentative_quality.logical_relevance: High - all premises directly support the thesis
argumentative_quality.premise_acceptability: Moderate - some premises rely on phenomenological intuitions and Aristotelian assumptions

distinctions_drawn: object-directed emotion vs mere physiological response
explicit_definitions_given: pre-named action: action caused directly by occurant emotion without belief-desire pair
post-named state: retroactive conceptualization of emotion into belief-desire pair
arational action: intentional action lacking belief-desire pair but having object-directedness

dialectical_engagement.objection_handling: Explicitly addresses the objection that arational actions collapse into reflexes, and resolves it by distinguishing object-directedness from reflex.
objections_raised: Moral culpability is impossible without belief-desire pair

method_and_evidence.evidence_type: Conceptual analysis, phenomenological description, counterexample (striking in rage), appeal to virtue ethics
named_thought_experiments: Agent striking another in a burst of pre-named rage

philosophical_orientation.grounding: Analytic philosophy of action with Aristotelian virtue ethics
philosophical_orientation.thematic_focus: Intentionality, moral responsibility, emotion and action

structural_organization.structure_type: Dialectical progression: thesis (Davidson) -> antithesis (Hursthouse) -> synthesis (revised intentionality)

summary_of_core_decisions: The essay argues that Hursthouse's arational actions undermine Davidson's belief-desire theory but do not collapse into reflexes. It resolves the normative dilemma by introducing indirect accountability through preventative emotion moderation, and proposes a dual-aspect theory of intentionality that accommodates affective, object-directed emotions.

thesis_commitment.conclusion_type: Revisionist - proposes a revised framework of intentionality
